bridges.description: Whether the universe’s beginning, apparent design, and moral truths together are best explained by a supreme being.
Whether a beginning of the universe calls for a cause beyond space, time, and matter.
Whether life-permitting order is best explained by an intelligent source.
Whether objective moral truths require a grounding explanation and whether God supplies it.
Whether abductive comparison can identify God as the best explanation without claiming certainty.
Whether the offered case leaves God unproved and critical nonbelief justified.
Whether the proposed spaceless, timeless, immaterial personal cause is coherent.
Whether natural selection, variable constants, or a multiverse undercut the design inference.
Whether moral values arise in minds while consequences can still be assessed objectively.
Whether the affirmative has supplied enough evidence and argument to meet its burden.

sections.title: Cosmic origin and causal explanation

sections.title: Design, fine-tuning, and alternatives

moves.speaker: Adam Lloyd Johnson
moves.claim: The universe had a beginning and therefore had a cause.
moves.warrant: Whatever has a beginning must have a cause, and the universe had a beginning.
moves.inference: A cause of the universe is required.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: This is the smallest contiguous passage containing both premises and the stated conclusion of Johnson’s first-cause argument.

moves.attributionRationale: The passage falls within Johnson’s uninterrupted opening after his named handoff.
moves.importanceRationale: This is one of the three principal constructive lines in the cumulative case.

burdenContact.rationale: It supplies the causal premise for moving from cosmic beginning to a transcendent explanation.

precisionClarity.rationale: The premises and conclusion are stated plainly, making the inferential structure unusually easy to audit.

calibrationCharity.rationale: The conclusion is limited to a cause, but calling the causal maxim universal is more confident than the supplied defense warrants.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The two premises and causal conclusion form a clear valid syllogism, though the universal causal premise is left without a qualification about kinds of beginnings.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Johnson states the beginning and causation premises but supplies no scientific support here for the universe’s beginning or for applying ordinary causation universally.

responsiveness.rationale: As an opening constructive, it directly addresses the cosmic-origin route and clearly establishes the proposition Barker later challenges.

moves.claim: A supreme being is offered as the best explanation of the universe’s cause.
